FOREWORD 

ibis Indian Standard (Part 2) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Bulk 
Handhng Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering 
Division Council. 

In industries such as steel, thermal power, cement, etc, uniform quality of the raw material plays an important role 
in the quality of the product and also for the optimum operation of the plant. The raw material is therefore first 
stacked, blended and then reclaimed for feeding to the plant for further processing. Stacking is done by stackers 
and various types of stackers are used for this purpose. 

A stacker consists of a system of belt conveyors and extended stacker boom through which material is stacked in 
the form of heap. The pile of the material may consist of the same material but in different size or may consist of 
different material depending upon requirements. The stacked material is then reclaimed by the re-claimer and 

loaded onto the conveyor system for feeding to the plant. 

This standard is published in three parts. The other parts of this standard are: 
Part 1 Genera! requirements. 
Part 3 Data to be furnished by the manufacturer/supplier. 

The formukuion of this standard is with a view to provide guidelines for adoption of uniform approach by the 

purchaser and the manufacturer/supplier. 



IS 15367 (Part 2 ) : 2003 



Indian Standard 

BULK HANDLING EQUIPMENT— STACKER 

(RAIL MOUNTED) 

PART 2 DATA TO BE FURNISHED BY THE PURCHASER 



1 SCOPE 

This standard (Part 2) lays down the data for various 
types of rail mounted mobile stackers to be furnished 
by the purchaser. This standard does not cover the rail 
mounted combined stacker cum re-claimer. 

2 TECHNICAL PARTICULARS TO BE 
FURNISHED BY THE PURCHASER 

2.1 Main Features 

a) Type of stacker, and 

b) Make. 

2.2 Stacking Capacity (t/h) 

a) Rated (guaranteed) capacity, and 

b) Designed capacity. 

2.3 Wind Velocity (km/h) 

a) Operating, 

b) Non-operating, and 

c) Strom. 

2.4 Type and Capacity of Stock Pile 

2.5 Dimensions of Stock Pile 

a) Height (m), 

b) Width at stock pile base (m), and 

c) Length at stock pile base (m). 

2.6 Long Travel Rail Details 

a) 1 ype, 

b) Size, and 

c) Track gauge (m). 

2.7 Length of Runway (m) 

2.8 Boom Conveyor and Yard Conveyor 

a) Boom reach (m), 

b) Belt width (mm) and trough angle (degree), 

c) Slewing and luffmg range of boom, 

d) Distance between top of rail to bottom of pile, 

e) Conveyor belt specification, 

f) Walkways 

1 ) to be provided — one side/both sides, 

2) minimum width(s) (mm), and 



g) Any other important particulars such as yard 
conveyor details (belt width, trough angle, belt 
speed, conveyor layout, etc). 

3 MODE OF OPERATION 

a) Manual mode, 

b) Auto mode, and 

c) Semi-auto mode. 

4 PATTERN OF STOCK PILE BUILDING 

a) Chevron pattern, and 

b) Windrow pattern. 

NOTE — The stock pile may be trapezoidal, long conical and 
conical in formation. 

5 OTHER FEATURES 

a) Power supply voltage and frequency required/ 
available at site, 

b) Place of installation of machine and related 
geographical data, 

c) Lighting arrangements and type of lights in the 
stacking area, 

d) Type of communication system, 

e) Whether dust suppression is required or not, 

f) Material characteristics 

1) Density, 

2) Size to be handled, and 

3) Moisture contents. 

6 PAINTING SPECIFICATION 

a) Type, 

b) Shade, and 

c) Dry flim thickness. 

7 DETAILS OF MAIN ELECTRICAL ITEMS 

a) Power supply available 6.6.kV/3.3.kV/415V, 
and 

b) Battery limit of power supply. 

8 GENERAL 

a) Total capacity of stock pile in tonnes on each 

side; 

b) Top and bottom width of stock pile; 

c) Foundation type: Sleeper/Continuous footing; 



!S 15367 (Part 2 ) : 2003 

d) Drainage arrangement considered; h) Annunciation considered for control room of 

e) Stock pile area preparation, that is hard strata plant, 

included/excluded from scope; j) High tension (HT) transformer type and cap; 

t) Terminal point for: k) Power cable reeling drum (CRD) size; 

! ) Power supply, and m) Trailing power cable size; 

2) Control supply; n) Control cable reeling drufn size, and 

g) Interlocking with other conveyors considered; p) Control cable size. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing 
the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed tp the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
'BIS Catalogue' and 'Standards: Monthly Additions'. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. ME 07 ( 0514 ).
